rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance when combining RNA and image data. This tests the core hypothesis that multimodal fusion improves accuracy. Using pca_n2000 (a standard RNA encoder) and resnet50 (a standard image encoder) with simple concatenation fusion allows isolating the effect of multimodal integration without complicating other factors.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000+resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly builds on the previous configuration, maintaining all other parameters constant, to evaluate a key design choice with minimal change, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with resnet50 image encoder achieve ~0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a larger, more powerful image encoder) while keeping RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation unchanged. This isolates the impact of the image encoder on performance, which is a key design choice with potential for significant gains. The experiment balances exploration of critical components with minimal parameter changes, directly addressing uncertainty about image encoder effectiveness.

The existing evidence shows that config_022 (singleprofile, no aggregation, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5353). The uncertainty lies in whether multiprofile settings could yield better results. Testing config_023 (multiprofile, same RNA/image encoders as config_022 but with weighted fusion) isolates the effect of profile setting and fusion method, providing critical insights into whether multiprofile configurations can surpass the current best while using the same encoders.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder with concat fusion (config_022) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.535). This experiment tests multiprofile settings with the same encoder and fusion method, isolating the effect of profile setting. Since multiprofile could leverage more data diversity, it's a key design choice to explore next, balancing exploitation of current strengths with potential gains from increased data complexity.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and imagenet_vit_l image encoders achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_024: 0.6287). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same setup improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is a logical extension of the current top-performing configuration and could clarify if weighted fusion offers gains without changing other critical parameters.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (a key design choice) while retaining weighted fusion (proven effective) could further improve performance. It balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of aggregation methods, prioritizing clarity about critical design impacts.

The existing evidence shows that config_025 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6352). This experiment tests switching to scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation while keeping multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder and aggregation method, which are critical factors. With limited budget, this comparison could reveal if these changes improve performance or confirm the current best configuration.

The existing evidence shows that config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) in the same setup could further improve performance. It directly compares encoder choices while keeping other critical parameters (multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) consistent, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder. This is the best use of the final experiment to either confirm or refute the potential of scgpt in this context.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests a similar setup but with scgpt RNA encoder and concat fusion, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice while maintaining transformer aggregation. It clarifies whether scgpt's performance differs from scvi_n200 in this context, balancing exploitation of proven aggregation methods with exploration of alternative encoders.
